subject: Processor list review & 30-day objection window — DPA execution plan
messages:
From: Jamie Laskin <jamie.laskin@tritonanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Amir Shah <amir.shah@tritonanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: DPA & processor transparency request

Hi Soojin,

We're starting procurement for our platform integration and legal asked for two narrow things before we can route to finance: 1) the latest executed DPA (or redlines) and 2) a current subprocessor roster with your planned notification cadence and the objection process.

Specifically, they're asking whether Redwood provides a notification window for new subprocessors (e.g. 30/45 days), whether customers can object, and what the escalation path looks like. Also need to confirm EU data transfer protections (SCCs / transfer mechanism).

Can you share those artifacts and a recommended path to execution (DocuSign or AdobeSign)? If there's a standard procurement timeline you expect, that would help us coordinate internal approvals.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Jamie
Legal Operations
Triton Analytics
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Laskin <jamie.laskin@tritonanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA & processor transparency request

Thanks Jamie — appreciate the clarity.

Quick summary of what I can share right away: attached is the current DPA with our latest redlines (Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx) and the current subprocessor roster (subprocessor_list_2027-04.csv). Our standard approach is:
- Notification window: 30 days prior notice for non-critical additions.
- Objection: customers have 30 days from notice to raise objections with a specific, documented basis.
- Escalation: if an objection is raised we escalate to our Privacy & Security review (internal SLA 5 business days) and then to commercial for remediation/mitigation; if unresolved, we provide an exit path for the impacted workload.

For EU transfers we rely on the EU SCCs (standard contractual clauses) layered in the DPA; if you require a particular addendum or local wording, let us know and we can discuss.

Plan for execution: we can push the final DPA via DocuSign. I'll prep the envelope once we align on the objection window and any carve-outs for regulated subprocessors (e.g., hosting partners vs analytics vendors).

Would you prefer a 30- or 45-day notice in writing? We commonly negotiate 30 days for security-conscious customers but will note any carve-outs.

On a separate note: included DPA has a short redline around Section 6 (data transfers) to call out SCCs and a reference to our subprocessor policy.

— Soojin
Head of Privacy & Compliance (contracts)
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: recommended language for notice & objection

On Tue, Apr 27, 2027 at 10:08 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Jamie — appreciate the clarity.

Sharing suggested contract language for the DPA redlines and a short playbook for procurement:

1) Notification window: firm 30-day notice for new subprocessors with a clause that Redwood will provide the subprocessor type, location, and data access justification in the notice.
2) Objection mechanics: customer must provide written objection within 30 days with specific reasons; Redwood will engage within 5 business days and propose mitigations (e.g., additional safeguards, contractual constraints, or alternate routing).
3) Emergency additions: for critical security patches or immediate infra changes, allow accelerated notification ("as soon as practicable") with post-notification retroactive review — but limit to documented emergencies and notify customer security contact immediately.
4) Escalation ladder: privacy -> security -> commercial -> CTO if unresolved after 15 business days. Offer temporary mitigation or sandboxing for impacted data while remediation is worked out.

For EU transfers, call out SCCs plus our internal audit evidence (SOC2 summary) in a single appendix to speed legal review.

If you want, I can inline these as redline text in Section 3.2 and Section 6 and we can route for signature. Also confirm DocuSign envelope settings: signer order (customer legal -> customer procurement -> Redwood privacy -> Redwood commercial).

-Karthik
VP, Product & Commercial Operations
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Laskin <jamie.laskin@tritonanalytics.com>, Amir Shah <amir.shah@tritonanalytics.com>, legal@tritonanalytics.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processor list review & 30-day objection window — DPA execution plan

Jamie / Amir — thanks for the quick answers on scope. Per internal alignment with Karthik and Laura, here's the agreed path so we can close this week: 

1) Notice & objection: Redwood will provide a 30-day notice for routine subprocessor additions. Customers have 30 days to object in writing with a specific rationale.
2) Escalation & remediation: Redwood engages privacy & security within 5 business days. If unresolved, escalation ladder applies with a maximum 15-business-day commercial remediation period; we will offer mitigation or exit options where feasible.
3) EU transfers: DPA includes EU SCCs (see redline Section 6) and we will supply the SCC Annex and our SOC2 summary via Drive link.
4) Signature flow: we'll send the final DPA via DocuSign (embedded link below). Signer order: Customer Legal -> Customer Procurement -> Redwood Privacy -> Redwood Commercial.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx (redlines), subprocessor_list_2027-04.csv (current roster).
DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/embedded/abcdef123456
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f

Next steps for Triton: confirm you accept the 30-day window (or propose a single carve-out) and confirm the signing order. Once I have that I'll send the DocuSign envelope and the DPA will be ready for signature.

If you'd like a 15-minute sync to walk through the subprocessor roster I can set one up — otherwise we'll proceed by email.

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Head of Privacy & Compliance (contracts)
Redwood Inference
